You estimate your annual income. You use the worksheet on Form 1040 ES to estimate your tax based on your estimated income. You divide by 4 and you make your quarterly payments by the deadlines.

Note that the way the rules works, you will not owe underwithholding penalties as long as your income has increased and you withhold at least as much as you paid in taxes the prior year. So you might want to simply estimate based on what you paid last year and by next year you'll have a better idea of how to,estimate everything. Bear in mind you still want to try to figure out what you will owe, since it sucks to find in April that you owe more money but don't have it.

If you have other regular income subject to withholding, you can also ignore quarterly filings and simply fill out a new W-4 to withhold extra amounts. If you do this, you still need to figure put how much tax you think you will owe. Then divide that amount by the remaining pay periods in the year and overwithhold that additional amount.

Can't really help you with sales tax (I assume you just keep records, calculate the tax on the sales and then send money in as your state requires).

For your income tax question, look at the worksheet on page 8 of the Form 1040 ES to which I linked. Now take the total you expect from both restaurant jobs. Add them together. Now you need to figure out the profits from the photography business. That will require you to guess. Your photography business should only be taxed on the profits, too. So you will need to consult Schedule C. Determine the profits, then add that to the amount from the restaurants. Then you need to fill out the rest of the Form 1040 ES worksheet.

Note that you can deduct business expenses on Schedule C in calculating your profit even if you do not itemize deductions on Schedule A (that is, you can still use the standard deduction if that is better for you).
